title: Snapshot concordance checklist and upgrade safety plan
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic, component-aware approach to creating concordant snapshots for private deployments (VPC/on-prem), plus a safety-first upgrade plan that uses those snapshots. Focus: minimize RPO, keep upgrade rollback simple, and avoid long windows of cross-service inconsistency.

Audience:
- Platform engineers who operate private deploys
- Solutions engs doing customer upgrades
- SREs running DR drills

Goals and constraints:
- Target RTO <= 15m for control plane + core inference traffic in single-zone failures; RPO <= 5m for stateful components where possible.
- Many customers use S3-compatible object store (MinIO) + etcd/KV + Postgres (hot-standby) + model artifacts on local PVs.
- We must produce an ordered snapshot manifest that ties object-store snapshots to DB WAL positions and KV revision ids.

High-level strategy (concordant snapshots):
1) Quiesce and quiesce-tolerant capture: where possible, briefly quiesce writes. For services that can't be fully paused, record a short, well-defined "capture window" and attach clocks/wal/sequence metadata.
2) Snapshot manifest: for each capture, produce a manifest describing component snapshot ids and validation metadata: timestamps (RFC3339), checksums, DB LSN/WAL positions, etc.
3) Atomic publish: upload manifest to agreed object store prefix with a sequence number and "complete" marker (manifest-<ts>.json + .complete). Consumers only use manifests with complete marker present.
4) Verification pass: automated validator that pulls manifest and validates checksums and LSN monotonicity. Failure blocks promotion or cutover.

Manifest example (human-readable excerpt):
- manifest_id: snap-20250212-1032
- created_at: 2025-02-12T10:32:18Z
- components:
  - postgres: pg_dump: s3://minio/backups/pg/snap-20250212-1032.sql.gz, lsn: 0/1A2B3C, checksum: sha256:...
  - kvstore: etcd-snapshot: s3://minio/backups/etcd/snap-20250212-1032.db, revision: 45212, checksum: sha256:...
  - model-artifacts: s3://minio/backups/models/20250212/, manifest-checksum: sha256:...
  - cache-kv: redis-rdb: s3://minio/backups/redis/rdb-20250212.rdb, migrated: no
  - infra: terraform-state: s3://minio/tfstate/private-deploy/terraform.tfstate.gz, version: 20250212-7f3b

Primary capture checklist (pre-snapshot):
- Confirm remote-state backend reachable and unlocked (terraform state lock healthcheck).
- Turn off non-essential background tasks (analytics exporters, heavy reindex jobs).
- Sync NTP across nodes; ensure clock skew < 2s.
- Notify dependent services (3rd-party connectors) of short pause window.
- Run quick health smoke (admin /health endpoints).

Snapshot capture steps (operator playbook):
1) Lock write gate or shift traffic: redirect ~90% of requests to canary or read-only mode if supported.
2) Trigger DB checkpoint and start pg_basebackup or LVM snapshot depending on deployment. Record LSN immediately.
3) Trigger etcd snapshot (etcdctl snapshot save). Record revision.
4) Flush object-store multipart uploads and perform object-store consistency check (s3api list-objects + etag checks).
5) Tar model artifact dirs and push to object-store with checksum.
6) Capture terraform remote state (terraform state pull > /tmp/tfstate-<id>.json) and record its checksum.
7) Compose manifest with the above metadata and upload to s3 prefix, then create manifest.complete marker.
8) Run verifier: checksum, LSN monotonicity, file presence. If verifier fails, mark manifest.failed and escalate.

Verification harness (automation notes):
- Implement a small service 'snap-verify' that accepts a manifest URL and returns pass/fail with detailed diffs.
- Verify steps: object presence, checksums, pg LSN reachable (can replay WAL to LSN), etcd revision matches, tfstate checksum stable.
- Wire the verifier to our alerting channel; failing manifests cannot be used for DR cutover.

Terraform module notes (compatibility and upgrade guardrails):
- Keep provider versions pinned in a root module (aws/minio/rook-core etc.). Avoid implicit provider upgrades during customer upgrades.
- Introduce a snapshot-lifecycle module that exposes: snapshot_policy, retention_days, manifest_prefix, verification_lambda (or pod) target. This centralizes naming and ACLs.
- Remote state migration: when upgrading TF module major versions, do a two-step plan: (a) terraform plan with -target for new module resources, (b) state mv with explicit terraform state mv commands. Document state mv mappings in PRs.
- TF state locking: ensure DynamoDB (or equivalent) locks are monitored. Add a pre-upgrade check that reads lock table age and aborts if stale locks present.
- Example safer workflow to introduce new snapshot module with zero-downtime: create new module with new names, replicate snapshots for one cycle, and then switch manifest pointer to new prefix in a controlled rollback window.

TF operator commands cheat-sheet (on admin bastion):
- terraform init -backend-config="bucket=..."
- terraform state pull > /tmp/tfstate.json   # inspect before any mutation
- terraform plan -target=module.snapshot -out=upgrade.tfplan
- terraform apply "upgrade.tfplan"
- terraform state mv module.old_snapshot.module.resource module.new_snapshot.module.resource  # document exact mappings

Upgrade safety plan (pre-upgrade, during, post-upgrade):
Pre-upgrade:
- Confirm last 3 manifests passed verification and are younger than 24h.
- Take an ad-hoc manual manifest (call it fallback-manifest) and tag it retained-for-rollbacks.
- Run full smoke tests against staging cutover using fallback-manifest restore.
- Ensure capacity for rolling model-download bursts (network egress/caching) is available.
- Confirm on-call & escalation roster for 72h window.

During upgrade (stepwise):
- Step 0: Announce maintenance window and set traffic shaping to 50%->10% paths.
- Step 1: Apply infra-only terraform changes first (non-stateful modules). Wait 5m+ health check.
- Step 2: Deploy snapshot-lifecycle changes in passive mode (creates new objects but does not change manifest pointer). Validate a full manual snapshot cycle.
- Step 3: Switch manifest pointer during low-traffic epoch (10–20m window). Wait for verifier green.
- Step 4: Promote servers gradually and monitor 1m, 5m, error-rate, tail-latency dashboards.

Rollback plan (fast path):
- If verifier fails or error-rate spike > 3x baseline for 10m: revert manifest pointer to fallback-manifest (atomic rename of pointer file).
- If terraform upgrade created new resources that break rollback, run documented terraform state mv to move resources back then apply a restricted plan to recreate old resources in-place.
- If DB incompatibility detected, restore Postgres from the pre-upgrade pg_dump saved in the manifest and replay WALs until last-consistent LSN. This is slow; preferred to use the manifest pointer to rebuild.

DR drill scenarios (recommended cadence):
- Weekly: manifest creation + verifier run (automated).
- Monthly: single-component restore (e.g., etcd or PG) to staging cluster.
- Quarterly: full restore from manifest (object-store + DB + KV + model fetch), then run full smoke harness.

Failure modes and mitigations (short list):
- Partial snapshot (missing objects): manifest rejected by verifier; roll forward with next snapshot. If operator error, run targeted re-snapshot for missing components.
- TF remote-state drift: do immediate terraform state pull and compare with expected; re-import resources if drift accepted.
- Large model artifact uploads timeout: use multipart and smaller chunk sizes; ensure upload retry and resumability.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Should the manifest pointer be a simple object (manifest-pointer.txt) or use a small metadata service? Tradeoffs: object pointer is simple and consistent across airgapped setups; metadata service enables richer checks.
- Define retention policy for fallback manifests (how many to keep, legal retention).
- Add support for cryptographic signing of manifests (GPG or KMS).

Appendix: quick restore checklist (operator):
1) Identify manifest to use (manifest-id).
2) Pull manifest and run local verifier once more.
3) Restore terraform state to a recovery workspace: terraform init && terraform state push /tmp/tfstate-<id>.json (manual and only after review).
4) Restore etcd: etcdctl snapshot restore <file> --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd --initial-cluster=...
5) Restore Postgres: restore base backup and replay WALs to LSN in manifest.
6) Restore object-store artifacts to object store used in target cluster (allow overwrite).
7) Start control-plane components in passive mode; run smoke tests; promote traffic.

Notes to self / operator hints:
- Keep manifests small and human-readable; we will always need a quick grep to find LSNs and TF checksums.
- Automate as much verification as possible; manual restores are expensive and error-prone.
- During customer-facing upgrades, prefer to orchestrate manifest pointer changes during low-activity windows (night/weekend) unless SLA demands otherwise.

If this looks reasonable, next actions:
- Convert the manifest schema above into a JSON schema and add to Confluence (ticket JIRA-DR-342).
- Prototype snap-verify as a tiny Go tool that runs in a pod and returns structured diagnostics.
- Draft terraform module API (snapshot-lifecycle) and open an RFC PR for review.

Last edited by: Aisha Raman
